Ryan (CTO): Quick follow-up from the runtime portion of todays all-hands. Start posting any small Qs here so we can consolidate for the leadership FAQ.
Sophie (Runtime Eng): I'll answer infra/batching/kernel questions. If it's about product UX for batch knobs, ping Maya.
Kai (Kernel): Re: the new fused-attn prototype, we measured ~1.6x perf on 8k seq in microbenchmarks. Still working on stability.
Jules (EngOps): High level Q: when we say "autoshrink batch" what metric triggers it? queue length, p95 wait, or a hybrid?
Sophie (Runtime Eng): Hybrid. Primary signal is queue inter-arrival time + current SLO tag. If inter-arrival > T_wait and latency SLO active => shrink. If overall throughput target active => hold larger batches and accept some latency.
Maya (Product): For Console UX, we want a simple toggle: "Throughput-first" / "Latency-first" + advanced link to per-route knobs. That maps to the runtime signals Sophie mentioned.
Ryan (CTO): How about fallback order under pressure? short list pls.
Kai (Kernel): Fallback order we tested: 1) kernel swap to lower-memory kernel (no model change), 2) reduce batch join window (faster answer, smaller throughput), 3) model-variant fallback (quantized), 4) regional fallback. Kernel swaps are <100ms in our tests.
Anonymous: Are kernel swaps just switching PTX/cu kernel variants or loading totally different kernels? Any warm-up cost?
Kai (Kernel): Mostly selecting alternate kernels already JITed in memory. If not JITed, we do a quick JIT which can add ~200-400ms on first use. We're investing in pre-warming heuristics for common seq/bs combos.
Jules (EngOps): Ops concern: first-JIT spikes could show up as p95 blips. Can we gate JITs behind a canary pool?
Sophie (Runtime Eng): Yes, plan is canary-first deploy for any new kernel variant. Also will propagate binary cache across nodes to avoid repeated JITs.
Maya (Product): Customer question: will Optimize suggest the fallbacks automatically or just goals?
Sophie (Runtime Eng): Optimize will surface recommendations (e.g., quantize model X, enable prefix caching) and simulate estimated token-cost delta. Auto-apply will be opt-in and require canary approval.
Jules (EngOps): Small config snippet request for internal docs: want a minimal example of a route-level config that toggles latency vs throughput.
Sophie (Runtime Eng): Paste below minimal YAML we discussed:
```yaml
route: /chat/fast
priority: latency
batching:
  max_wait_ms: 12
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
fallbacks:
  - type: kernel_swap
  - type: batch_reduce
    params:
      min_batch: 1
  - type: model_variant
    params:
      tag: quant-8
```
Jules (EngOps): Nice. I'll add that to the runbook.
Ryan (CTO): Two asks: Sophie/Kai, drop a short PR with the kernel-affinity prototype notes. Maya, confirm timeline for Console flag. Jules, add follow-ups to the tracker.
Ops-bot: Follow-up created: "ah-runtime-kernel-batching-actions" assigned to Sophie, Kai, Maya, Jules.
Maya (Product): Timeline: feature-flagged Console controls -> beta in 6w, GA in 12w (tentative).
Kai (Kernel): Will post kernel perf microbench results to the kernel channel tomorrow. Expect a shorttable of seq-len x batch-size perf.
Sophie (Runtime Eng): I'll also add the fallback decision matrix to the internal docs by EOD Friday.
Ryan (CTO): Great. If anyone else has short Qs, drop them here rather than email. We'll fold into the FAQ. :slightly_smiling_face:
